summary: Source-anchored research for explain multiKeyPaths interpretation. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: An empty per-key list does not prove that the source document path contains no array. A positional key such as e.0 can read e[0] from an array without generating multiple index keys, so its multiKeyPaths entry can be empty while e is an array. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-21)

multiKeyPaths is per indexed key, while isMultiKey describes the index as a whole. Thus isMultiKey: true can coexist with one key having an empty list while another key has a non-empty list; an empty list means no multikey path component is recorded for that key, not that the whole index is non-multikey. (high confidence)

For an IXSCAN, multiKeyPaths is an object whose keys are those in the index key pattern and whose values are arrays of the paths (prefixes of the indexed field) that cause the index to be multikey. For example, with index {a: 1, b: 1} and a document {a: 5, b: [1, 2, 3]}, isMultiKey is true with a: [] and b: ['b']; an empty array means that indexed key has no multikey path even if the index as a whole is multikey. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-23115 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-15086

MongoDB issue SERVER-130777 reports a narrow resumable index-build failure where a concurrent array write can be lost from multikey state, leaving explain to report isMultiKey: false and causing a matching array document to be missed. The issue lists MongoDB 6.0.0, 7.0.0, and 8.0.0 as affected and was unresolved in code review as of 2026-10-12. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12)

multiKeyPaths is index path-level metadata: it describes which prefixes of the indexed fields cause the index to be multikey. The query planner uses this path-level multikey information to get tighter index bounds by assigning additional predicates to the index, and those resulting bounds appear in the IXSCAN's indexBounds, so read multiKeyPaths and indexBounds together. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-15086 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-23115
